identification.notes: Advertisements contain flags and the IDM local name, not the 0x00FA service UUID. The primary service and its characteristics are learned only through post-connect GATT discovery.

device.name: iDotMatrix
device.notes:
Multi-size RGB LED pixel-matrix display (text, images, GIF, effects, timers, schedules and one-pixel graffiti). No pairing required. Post-connect public GATT captures identify primary service 0x00FA, with characteristic 0xFA02 supporting write and write-without-response and 0xFA03 supporting notify only. Advertisements themselves carry flags and the IDM name, not this service UUID.
Framed upload protocol — 16-byte header per 4096-byte payload chunk:
  [0-1]  total frame length, header included (uint16 LE)
  [2]    command type: 1=GIF, 2=Image, 3=Text/MultiColor, 6=Phrase
  [3]    sub-type: always 0x00 in framed uploads (sub-type 0x02 exists
         only in the short MultiColor/Phrase commands below)
  [4]    chunk flag: 0=first, 2=continuation
  [5-8]  total payload length, excluding all headers (uint32 LE)
  [9-12] CRC32 of the payload only, excluding all headers (LE)
  [13-14] time/delay (uint16 LE)
  [15]   speed/type byte
  [16+]  payload
BLE chunking: 509 bytes when MTU negotiated, else 18 bytes; 20 ms/chunk for GIF/image, 50 ms/chunk for text. Notify response: [?,0,cmd_type,sub_type,status] with status 0=invalid, 1=next-chunk, 2=error, 3=finished. Public captures independently confirm LE lengths and payload-only CRC32 on 0xFA02. The full 0x1010 frame length is byte-palindromic, so short frames are the useful endian check. Display sizes (from the app's screen-size table): 1010=10x10, 1001=1x100, 1116=16x11, 1318=18x13, 1619=19x16, 1920=20x19, 2020=20x20 (default), 2010=10x20, 3010=10x30, 3820=20x38. Square 16x16 / 32x32 / 64x64 panels also exist and use this same IDM-/0x00FA protocol family. Upload format: public clients upload encoded PNG or GIF files, which the device decodes; it crops rather than resizes. Separately, public graffiti vector 0a 00 05 01 00 ff 00 00 1f 1f draws one red RGB888 pixel at (31,31). A full raw framebuffer remains unobserved. Text glyph width varies by device/font. CONFIDENCE: primary service, characteristic properties, framing header, CRC coverage and the one-pixel command are capture-backed. Command type 6=Phrase and still-image material fields remain app-derived. Service 0xFEE9 is retained only as negative evidence below: it is an unused BLE library default, not an alternative hardware transport. Evidence: 8none1/idotmatrix public captures and decoding notes, derkalle4/python3-idotmatrix-library, fbnlrz/homeyidotmatrix docs/idm.md, plus the vendor app's upload and command builders.
Short command protocol — primary service 0x00FA: unframed length-prefixed byte commands ([len, 0x00, cmd, ...]) written to characteristic 0xFA02, with acks/notifications on 0xFA03. Name prefix "IDM-".
APP-PROVEN-UNUSED — service 0xFEE9 with characteristics d44bc439-abfd-45a2-b575-925416129600/9601: these UUIDs are merely the shipped defaults of the app's third-party BLE library (a third-party BLE library's default options); the app overrides them at init with service 0x00FA / characteristic 0xFA02, so they are dead config in the app. That UUID pair is also a stock NXP BLE-UART demo pair reused by many unrelated products, and no public source has observed it on iDotMatrix hardware. Kept below for completeness — do not rely on 0xFEE9 being present.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. The vendor app adds a cloud content library, but none of it is required to connect to and drive the display.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

enter.notes: In-band over JieLi RCSP on ae01/ae02. Whether this part is single-backup (reboots into a loader, client reconnects) or dual-backup (updates in place) is not established, and a session-dependent component of the exchange is unsolved (235/256 two-byte probes elicit responses), so no entry bytes are known.

image.notes: The app bundles two images (TR2401R006_01_01_ota_mi.bin, TR2401R007_02_01_ota_mi.bin); they stay in the app. It also runs a version check against the vendor cloud (manage.heaton.com.cn).

dfu.notes: From the app (embedded JieLi OTA SDK) and fbnlrz/homeyidotmatrix docs/AE-SERVICE.md (hardware-probed service, not a completed update). The app's hard-coded AES key encrypts its cloud HTTP bodies and is not shown to touch the OTA wire payloads.

helpful_urls.description: HACS integration driving iDotMatrix BLE pixel boards locally (native adapter or Bluetooth proxy).
helpful_urls.title: adriantukendorf/iDotMatrix-HomeAssistant (HACS)

helpful_urls.description: No vendor manual is published anywhere that resolves — iDotMatrix ship a QR code to an app and nothing else. This reverse-engineered client is the working documentation for the protocol.
helpful_urls.title: derkalle4/python3-idotmatrix-client

remaining_unknowns: Static-image (type 2) header bytes 13-15 are read from the vendor app's image builder, which mirrors its GIF builder; no public capture of a type-2 upload exists to confirm the device honours display_seconds for stills. The public PNG path (derkalle4 image.py, Homey §4.16) uses a different header-less DIY layout after enter_diy_mode instead.
Whether the device accepts material_type values other than 12 and 13 is untested; the app sends only those two.

characteristics.name: Data Write/Read
characteristics.notes: Library-default write characteristic, unused by the app (overridden with 0xFA02 at init). The framing block is repeated here only for the record — the authoritative declaration, with the upload commands, is on 0xFA02. The framed protocol that would run here — and does run on 0xFA02 — is a 16-byte header (length field at [0-1] is uint16 LITTLE-endian) + up to 4096-byte payload per frame; CRC32 (java.util.zip.CRC32) over the whole data payload. Framing verified on 0xFA02 by 8none1, derkalle4 gif.py and Homey docs/idm.md §4.17, and app-side in the vendor app's GIF upload path.

characteristics.name: Data Notify
characteristics.notes: Library-default notify characteristic, unused by the app. The transfer-progress response format is verified on 0xFA03, and app-side in the vendor app's GIF upload path.

services.name: iDotMatrix Data Service (app-proven-unused)
services.notes: These UUIDs are the shipped defaults of the app's third-party BLE library (its default options); the app overrides them at init with service 0x00FA / characteristic 0xFA02, so this service is dead config and no public source has observed it on iDotMatrix hardware. The d44bc439-…-9600/9601 pair is also a stock NXP BLE-UART demo pair reused by unrelated products. On all hardware-documented units the framed protocol described here runs over 0xFA02 alongside the short commands.

services.name: JieLi RCSP / OTA Service
services.notes: Jieli (杰理) OTA stack (the app embeds Jieli's OTA SDK, which is public as Jieli-Tech/Android-JL_OTA). ae00 is JieLi's stock RCSP service, shared by every JieLi product, so it marks a JieLi SoC, not this panel and not update mode. It is the update path: a generic client lists it read-only. Not yet unlocked publicly — a session-dependent component is unsolved (235/256 two-byte inputs elicit responses). Evidence: fbnlrz/homeyidotmatrix docs/AE-SERVICE.md (hardware-probed). The app bundles two OTA firmware images (TR2401R006_01_01_ota_mi.bin, TR2401R007_02_01_ota_mi.bin), so firmware artifacts do exist inside it. The hard-coded ASCII AES-256-CBC key with IV = 16 x ASCII '0' (in the app's crypto helper) is consumed by its cloud HTTP encryption — request/response bodies for manage.heaton.com.cn, including the OTA version-check call — and is NOT demonstrated to encrypt OTA wire payloads; no wire capture ties it to this service.

draw_pixel.description: Draw one RGB888 pixel at zero-based x/y in graffiti mode. Capture-proven public vector: mode 0, red (255,0,0), at (31,31) is exactly 0a 00 05 01 00 ff 00 00 1f 1f. This establishes the short one-pixel command only; a full raw framebuffer remains unobserved.

mode.description: Graffiti mode 0, the only capture-observed value.

eco_mode.description: Eco mode with six config bytes (app-derived, not yet hardware-verified — byte semantics unknown)

joint.description: Joint/splice setting for multi-panel setups (app-derived, not yet hardware-verified)

locate.description: Locate device. This is a genuinely different frame from the short commands: not [len, 0x00, cmd, ...] but a 16-byte block whose first byte is 0x06 followed by ASCII 'LOCATE' and NUL padding (from the app's command builder). The bytes below are the PLAINTEXT — the app does not write them directly: its locate path AES-encrypts the block in place before the single BLE write, so the actual on-wire bytes are the 16-byte ciphertext, not this plaintext. App-derived only; no community/hardware source documents a locate command, so treat as unconfirmed.

mic_rhythm_command.description: Microphone rhythm control; first payload byte is mode+1 per app (app-derived, not yet hardware-verified). Shares cmd/sub 0x0B 0x80 with set_mic_type; the device dispatches on the frame's length byte (this one is length 0x06, two payload bytes) rather than on cmd/sub alone.

reset_step_1.description: Factory reset, step 1 of 2 — follow with reset_step_2 (Homey docs/idm.md; found by 8none1)

reset_step_2.description: Factory reset, step 2 of 2 — completes the reset started by reset_step_1

set_fullscreen_color.description: Fill the whole screen with one RGB colour (Homey docs/idm.md)

set_mic_type.description: Set hardware microphone type (app-derived, not yet hardware-verified). Shares cmd/sub 0x0B 0x80 with mic_rhythm_command; the device dispatches on the frame's length byte (this one is length 0x05, one payload byte) rather than on cmd/sub alone.

set_password.description: Set 6-digit password (000000-999999). Reset device to clear.

upload_gif_chunk.description: One frame of an animated-GIF upload, command type 1 — the same header as upload_image_chunk with 0x01 at byte 2. The hardware-verified public form (derkalle4 gif.py, 8none1's capture 10 10 01 00 … 05 00 0d) sends display time 5 and material type 13; the vendor app's GIF builder fills those two fields exactly as the image builder does. GIF bytes go as-is — the device decodes the file. Ack-gate on 0xFA03 between frames.

chunk_flag.description: 0 on the first frame of a file, 2 on every later frame.

crc32.description: CRC-32 (zlib) of the whole GIF file, repeated in every frame.

display_seconds.description: Seconds the GIF stays up in a rotation; 5 is what every hardware-verified client sends.

labels: plain upload (display time ignored, sent as 0)

packet_length.description: Total bytes of this frame, header included; encoder-filled, LITTLE-endian.

payload.description: Up to 4096 bytes of the GIF file, in order.

total_length.description: Length of the whole GIF file — the same value in every frame.

upload_image_chunk.description: One frame of a static-image (PNG file) upload, command type 2: [packet length u16 LE][0x02][0x00][chunk flag][total file length u32 LE][CRC32 of the whole file u32 LE][display seconds u16 LE] [material type][payload]. Send the frames in order and wait for the 0xFA03 ack (status 1) between them; the device decodes the PNG once all `total_length` bytes have arrived. The last three header fields were unstated until now: the vendor app's image builder writes the display time from its material-time picker (5/10/30/60/300 s) and the material-type byte it was handed — 12 for a plain upload, where the time is forced to 0, and 13 for a timed material. 8none1's app captures show the type-12 form (00 00 0c). App-derived for type 2 (derkalle4's PNG path uses a different, header-less DIY layout), so `reported`.

chunk_flag.description: 0 on the first frame of a file, 2 on every later frame.

crc32.description: CRC-32 of the whole file (zlib / java.util.zip.CRC32: reflected poly 0xEDB88320, init and xorout 0xFFFFFFFF) — over the file, not this frame, so no `auto` span role fits it; the client computes it once and repeats it in every frame.

display_seconds.description: Seconds the material stays up in a rotation; the app offers 5, 10, 30, 60 or 300 and sends 0 with material_type 12.

material_type.description: The app's material-type byte; 12 (0x0C) for a plain upload, 13 (0x0D) for a material shown for display_seconds.
labels: plain upload (display time ignored, sent as 0)

packet_length.description: Total bytes of this frame, header included (4112 for a full chunk); encoder-filled, LITTLE-endian — the byte-palindromic 0x1010 of a full chunk hides a byte swap until the last frame.

payload.description: Up to 4096 bytes of the PNG file, in order.

total_length.description: Length of the whole file across all frames — the same value in every frame.

verify_password.description: Verify 6-digit password, three 2-digit groups as bytes (app-derived, not yet hardware-verified)

characteristics.name: Notify/Ack Data
characteristics.notes: Notify-only channel: upload-progress responses and command acks (05 00 <cmd> <sub> 01) arrive here. Public GATT declarations have property byte 0x10 (notify), with no read property.

services.name: iDotMatrix Command/Upload Service (0x00FA)
services.notes: Public GATT captures list 0x00FA as a primary service and place the 0xFA02 and 0xFA03 characteristics beneath it. The protocol every public client speaks (derkalle4/python3-idotmatrix-library, nj-designs/go-idot, fbnlrz/homeyidotmatrix — hardware-verified) uses this service. The short length-prefixed commands below and the framed CRC32 upload protocol (16-byte header, length at [0-1] uint16 LE) both run on characteristic 0xFA02. Additional opcodes from Homey docs/idm.md: set-time 0b 00 01 80 …, clock 08 00 06 01 …, countdown 07 00 08 80 …, chronograph 05 00 09 80 …, scoreboard 08 00 0a 80 …, built-in effects [len, 0, 03, 02, style, 90, count, rgb…], music sync 06 00 00 02 …. Command acks arrive on 0xFA03 as 05 00 <cmd> <sub> 01. The vendor app confirms this configuration: it overrides its BLE library defaults with service 0x00FA + write characteristic 0xFA02 and sends the full short-command set below from its protocol builder.
